name: Buraco
description: Buraco is a popular Rummy-type card game family originating in South America, played with partnerships and featuring unique mechanics like the morto (extra hand). The main variants are Brazilian Buraco (Canastra/Biriba), Italian Burraco, and Argentinean Burako (tile version). Games are played with double decks and involve melding sequences to create canastas.

overview.description: Buraco is a popular Rummy-type card game family originating in South America, played with partnerships and featuring unique mechanics like the morto (extra hand). history.origins: Buraco originated in South America, probably in the 1940s, likely in Brazil or Argentina. The game evolved from Canasta and shares similarities with Samba. The name comes from Portuguese/Spanish and refers to the 'hole' or extra hand mechanic.
timeline: Mid-20th century: Spread throughout Brazil and Argentina
1990s: Italian variation Burraco became extremely popular in Italy
2000s-present: International tournaments and online play established
history.cultural: Buraco is one of the most popular card games in Brazil and Italy. In Brazil, it's commonly played in social clubs, bars, and family gatherings. Italian Burraco has competitive leagues and tournaments. The game bridges social classes and generations in both countries.
history.evolution: The game family has three main branches: Brazilian Buraco (also called Canastra, Biriba, Perida), Italian Burraco (with significant rule differences), and Argentinean Burako (played with tiles instead of cards). Each variant has developed unique rules while maintaining core mechanics.

setup.deck: 104-108 cards: two standard 52-card decks plus 0-4 jokers depending on variant
setup.dealing: Two 11-card mortos (extra hands) set aside. Each player receives 11 cards. Remaining cards form draw pile. Brazilian: 108 cards with 4 jokers; Italian: 104 cards no jokers; twos often wild.
setup.equipment: Double deck with jokers, score sheet, table space for melds

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach target score (typically 2000-3000 points) by melding sequences, creating canastas (7+ card sequences), and going out. Score points from melded cards plus bonuses.
rules.gameplay: Players draw and discard, melding sequences of 3+ consecutive cards of same suit. Wild cards (jokers/twos) can substitute. First player to empty hand takes a morto (11-card extra hand). Team can go out after taking morto and having at least one canastra. Play ends when team goes out or cards exhausted.
keyRules: Two 11-card mortos set aside for first players out
Melds are sequences of 3+ consecutive cards of same suit
Clean canastra (no wilds) scores more than dirty
Must have taken morto and have canastra to go out
Vulnerability rule: half target score needs minimum opening meld

strategy.basic: Focus on creating your first canastra early. Use wild cards wisely to complete sequences. Communicate with partner through discards. Take morto when you have a strong position.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been played. Coordinate with partner on which sequences to build. Time your go-out carefully - going out early may deny opponents their morto bonus. Manage vulnerability status.
strategy.advanced: Calculate optimal discard pile takes. Force opponents into difficult positions. Use closed vs open discard pile strategy depending on variant. Advanced card counting to predict opponent hands. Optimize meld layouts for maximum scoring.
tips: Always try to create at least one clean canastra
Save wild cards for critical sequence completions
Going out quickly can deny opponents morto bonus
Consider vulnerability when planning opening meld
In closed variants, discard pile is more risky
Track played cards to predict what opponents need

variations.name: Buraco Fechado (Closed Buraco)
variations.description: Variation where the discard pile is closed (only the top card is visible), sets of equal rank are allowed as melds, and a canastra of twos can score a higher bonus; going out only requires at least one canastra, not necessarily clean.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine overrides for this closed-pile variant are not yet encoded; implementers should adjust discard and meld rules based on this description.

variations.name: Alternative Target Scores
variations.description: Some groups play to a target of 2000 or 3500 points instead of the standard 3000, ending the match when a team reaches or passes the chosen total.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Target score alternatives are described here but not wired into engine constants; choose and apply the desired match target in implementation.

variations.name: Rounded Scoring to Tens
variations.description: In some tables all scores are rounded up to the nearest multiple of ten, for example 485 is recorded as 490 on the running score sheet.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Score rounding is handled at the scoring layer and is not yet represented as explicit engine overrides.

variations.name: No Vulnerability Requirement
variations.description: Some play without the vulnerability rule, so there is no minimum opening meld value even after a team has reached half of the target score.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Vulnerability and opening meld thresholds are not yet modeled as configurable engine constants for this variation.

variations.name: High-Value Jokers
variations.description: A common scoring variation treats each joker as worth 50 points instead of the standard 20, increasing the impact of wild cards in melds and in hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Per-card point values are described here but are not yet injected as separate scoring override data.

variations.name: No Jokers, Only Twos Wild
variations.description: Some play with no jokers in the deck so that only the twos act as wild cards, giving a 106-card pack while keeping the same meld structure.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deck composition for the no-joker variant is documented here but not yet expressed as a separate deck type or engine override.

variations.name: Alternative Canastra Bonuses
variations.description: Some groups score 150 points for a dirty canastra and 300 for a clean one, count a clean set of all eight cards of a rank as a canastra real worth 1000 points, or award extra bonuses for special cutting situations.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: These bonus and penalty tweaks are summarized here but not yet parameterized as explicit scoring override fields.

scoring.description: At the end of each hand both teams total the point values of their melded cards, subtract the values of cards left in hand, and apply bonuses and penalties for different types of canastras, going out, and unused mortos.
scoring.winCondition: Teams accumulate scores over multiple hands; when a team reaches or passes the target (normally 3000 points), the team with the higher total score wins the game.
